title: Refine dedicated capacity billing: continuous burst reconciliation and SLA credit amortization
creator: Alyssa Park
description:
Summary:
We need a robust reconciliation model for dedicated pool billing that (1) accurately attributes reserved throughput consumption vs. burst usage across tenants, (2) amortizes SLA credits so they are both predictable for accounting and fair for customers, and (3) tolerates partially degraded pools without producing negative billing artifacts or customer-facing quota regressions.

Why this work matters:
- Several customers reported unexpected invoice line items after transient pool slowdowns during maintenance windows.
- Current burst accounting is implemented as a simple token decrement per request and produces outlier negative balances when SLA credits and partial outages overlap.
- Finance requires a deterministic, auditable amortization method for SLA credits to close monthly invoices.

Goals / Success criteria:
- Final billing output matches a golden set (internal test fixture) for 99.99% of simulated workload traces across 30-day windows.
- No customer experiences a negative reserved balance on invoices; any temporary negative in the runtime is converted into explicit SLA credit entries visible in the invoice.
- Billing pipeline runs end-to-end within SLA for monthly processing (<= 3 hours for all tenants).

Acceptance criteria (technical):
- Implement continuous burst reconciliation that accumulates burst consumption into a time-bucketed ledger (1m and 1h windows) and reconciles against reserved throughput at the end of each hour.
- SLA credit amortization logic that: (a) classifies incident time as "full outage" or "degradation" using observed latency and error rates, (b) applies credit fraction proportional to measured impact and reserved share, and (c) writes standard accounting entries: CREDIT_SLA_AMORTIZED and CREDIT_SLA_IMMEDIATE (when required).
- Invoice generator includes detailed line items and a reconciliation report: reserved_used, burst_used, credit_amortized, credit_immediate, net_charge.
- Unit and integration tests cover corner cases: overlapping incidents, pool failover, tenant migration between pools mid-window.

High-level design decisions made so far:
- Ledger model: prefer append-only time-bucketed ledger (per-tenant, per-pool) for easier auditing and replay instead of moving balance counters. This supports deterministic monthly replays.
- Two-phase credits: immediate credits for incidents where SLA triggers and system confirms impact within 30m; amortized credits for longer running degradations that are reconciled hourly. This prevents invoice churn while still being fair.
- Negative-balance policy: do not emit negative invoice amounts; instead capture runtime negative into a "temporary SLO buffer" and convert to explicit credit line items at reconciliation time.

Technical design (implementation notes):
- New data structures: BurstLedgerRecord {tenant_id, pool_id, bucket_start_iso, reserved_consumed_tokens, burst_consumed_tokens, metadata_tags}. Stored in ClickHouse (existing billing cluster) with daily partitions.
- Reconciliation job: hourly batch job in billing-service that consumes BurstLedgerRecords and pool health events (from observability stream) to produce AccountingEntries appended to the monthly invoice CDC topic.
- SLA classifier: lightweight rule engine in billing-service using latency p99 thresholds and 5xx ratios with weights; ruled by config so PM/Finance can tune without deploys.
- Edge case: tenant migration mid-hour will produce two ledger rows; reconciliation must sum slices and attribute to correct tenant invoice during invoice assemble.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flagged roll-out in staging: enable ledger write and reconciliation in dry-run mode for 2 weeks. Compare output to current production pipeline using shadow run.
2) Canary: enable for <10 tenants (low-billing) for 1 billing cycle. Monitor discrepancies and finance sign-off.
3) Full enablement for all Dedicated pools after billing ops review.

QA & test plan:
- Create synthetic workload generator to produce 10k tenant traces with parameterized burstiness and controlled degradation windows.
- Create golden comparison harness: run legacy pipeline and new reconciliation; assert net_charge diff < 0.1% and identical line items format for >99.99% of tenants.
- Manual validation: finance to validate invoices for canary tenants against raw ledger.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Dedicated billing reconciliation" with metrics: hourly_reconciled_tenants, reconciliation_duration_p95, credit_amortized_total, negative_buffer_count.
- Alerts: reconciliation job failures, backlog growth > 6h, net_charge_variance_rate > 0.5% in a billing cycle.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Precision of amortization: do we amortize strictly proportional to reserved share or account level-of-service (e.g., burst-priority tenants)? Team recommends starting proportional to reserved share and adding weighting later if customers request differentiation.
- Storage choice: ClickHouse has good analytic properties but retention cost is non-trivial; should we downsample 1m buckets to 1h after 7 days? Proposed: downsample but retain full 1m for 14 days to support debugging.
- SLA classification sensitivity: tuning thresholds will be required; plan to expose controls to SRE/Finance.

Implementation tasks (rough):
- Add BurstLedger write path to serving runtime (ENG-27340) — Marcus to pair with runtime team.
- ClickHouse schema migration and retention policy (ENG-27343).
- Reconciliation worker (billing-service) + config-driven SLA classifier (ENG-27321-impl).
- Invoice generator changes and invoice line item format (finance-schema PR).
- End-to-end integration tests and golden harness (ENG-27345).

Notes on uniqueness vs existing tickets:
This ticket focuses on continuous time-bucketed ledger reconciliation, explicit amortization flows for SLA credits, and the negative-balance-to-credit-buffer conversion policy to avoid customer-facing anomalies. It differs from prior work that aggregated burst credits or normalized usage for SLA offsets by introducing a deterministic append-only ledger and configurable SLA classification that allows safe dry-runs and audits.

If you are reviewing: please read the acceptance criteria and high-level design and comment on any missing auditability requirements from Finance or any anticipated tiering impacts from Platform teams.
